text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Cape Verdean citizens will be allowed soon to work in Portugal on a temporary basis, according to an agreement signed by Prime Minister Antonio Guterres and Cape Verdean officials in the West African archipelago yesterday.
- Planning Minister Joao Cravinho will present a new law today which paves the way to open Portuguese telecommunications to free competition.

- Retail group Jeronimo Martins has decided not to invest in Hungary, preferring to focus instead on Poland and to expand its operations in Portugal. Hungary has relatively slow economic growth and already presents strong competition in retailing, a company source told the paper.
- Former prime minister Anibal Cavaco Silva said, ahead of Thursday's parliamentary debate on abortion, that it would be better to leave abortion legislation as it is.

- President Jorge Sampaio said he wanted a "peaceful and efficient" transfer of the territory of Macau to China in 1999. He was speaking after his arrival in Macau for a six-day visit before proceeding to China.
- Oporto Derivatives Exchange registered record volume yesterday.
